title: Chess vs Shogi
summary: Tony's normal chess army faces Fairy-Stockfish playing a full Shogi army on a 9x9 board. Stockfish follows Shogi rules (pieces promote in the last three ranks; captured pieces go to its hand and can be dropped back anywhere), while Tony follows chess rules with no drops. Stockfish drops captured pieces (rook on a1, bishop on f1, pawns), but Tony counterattacks and mates with a rook+knight double check (~12:53).
rules: Board is 9x9 to fit the Shogi setup.

Opponent (Black): full Shogi army — king, rook, bishop, 2 gold generals, 2 silver generals, 2 knights (shogi knight: only forward 2+1), 2 lances (forward any distance), 9 pawns (move AND capture 1 straight forward).
Shogi side promotes pieces entering/moving within its last three ranks (rook->dragon king, bishop->dragon horse, minors->gold-like).
Shogi side keeps captured pieces in hand and may drop them on empty squares as a move.
Player (White): standard chess army on the 9x9 board, plays by chess rules, no drops (exact placement of the chess army on 9 files is visual-only).
